lesson: TWO findings from the mandatory design pass (emil-design-eng, frontend-design), both real and both small. (1) THE REPLACED NOTICE IS STYLED AS AN ERROR. statement-explanation.tsx:59 renders it with role=alert and globals.css paints it with --kl-error and --kl-error-tint. But decision 0025 is explicit that a replaced-but-still-present batch's figures are LEGITIMATE - read and reported, not refused - so red plus an assertive alert tells the user something broke when nothing did. It is the same category mistake decision 0034 forbids for the Budget not-loaded state, which must never render as an error. This is advisory, accompanying valid content: use role=status, which is polite rather than interrupting, and give it an advisory treatment rather than the error palette. The design system has only error and success tokens today, so either add a warning token properly or keep the strong left border for prominence with a neutral ink/slate fill - what must not survive is red plus alert. The figures must stay the loudest thing in the panel; the notice sits beside them, impossible to miss without shouting over them. (2) REDUCED MOTION IS NOT RESPECTED for the new control. .statement-explanation-open has a transform scale(0.97) on :active, which is the right press feedback, but it is NOT listed in the prefers-reduced-motion block in globals.css - every other button in this file is (.exploration-actions button, .ask-preserve-actions button, .ask-suggestions button and the rest). Add it, so the new control follows the accessibility floor the file already holds. Do NOT change the tabular-nums and right-aligned numerics, the focus-visible ring or the press feedback itself - those are correct and are why the panel reads as financial rather than chatty.
source: design pass on the shipped explanation surface
